pages.title: Can I use a 60/40 salary split for my S corporation?
pages.seo_title: S Corp 60/40 Salary Rule: What to Use Instead
pages.description: Begin with a role inventory: billable work, sales, management and administration.

pages.title: Should my S corporation salary change when profit doubles?
pages.seo_title: S Corp Salary When Profit Increases
pages.description: Compare the current year with the year used in the last compensation review.

pages.title: Can I take S corporation distributions before running owner payroll?
pages.seo_title: S Corp Distributions Before Payroll: Correction Steps
pages.description: Prepare a dated list of draws, company-paid personal costs, wages and reimbursements.

pages.title: Does a part-time S corporation owner need reasonable compensation?
pages.seo_title: Part-Time S Corp Owner Salary: Duties and Hours
pages.description: Document the work performed for this corporation separately from work for another employer.

pages.title: Do two S corporation owners have to earn identical salaries?
pages.seo_title: Different S Corp Owner Salaries: Equal Ownership
pages.description: Prepare a responsibilities matrix for each owner, including revenue production, supervision, administration and time away from the business.

pages.title: Can an S corporation owner pay zero salary in a loss year?
pages.seo_title: Zero S Corp Salary in a Loss Year
pages.description: Determine why the business reports a loss and whether the owner still received cash or personal benefits.

pages.title: Should a real estate agent elect S corporation status after a strong commission year?
pages.seo_title: S Corp Election for Real Estate Agents: Recurring Profit
pages.description: Start with net commission income after ordinary operating expenses, rather than gross closings.

pages.title: Does paying myself more S corporation wages always reduce my total tax?
pages.seo_title: Higher S Corp Salary: Payroll Tax and Retirement Tradeoffs
pages.description: No. Payroll costs, retirement limits, QBI and other household facts can move the overall result in different directions.

pages.title: Can an S corporation pay a shareholder health insurance premium?
pages.seo_title: S Corp Shareholder Health Insurance: Payroll Handoff
pages.description: Identify who paid each premium, whether the corporation reimbursed the shareholder and whether the shareholder is subject to the more-than-2% rules.

pages.title: What evidence should I keep for an S corporation salary review?
pages.seo_title: S Corp Salary Documentation: Compensation Review File
pages.description: A useful file explains the owner's work, the market evidence used and the reason the selected wage fits.

pages.title: How should a business owner pay estimated tax on uneven income?
pages.seo_title: Estimated Taxes on Uneven Business Income
pages.description: Build a period-by-period profit schedule and include household wages, investment income and other activities.

pages.title: Does an estimated tax safe harbor mean I will not owe more in April?
pages.seo_title: Estimated Tax Safe Harbor vs April Balance Due
pages.description: Ask for two figures: the amount needed under an applicable payment safe harbor and the projected final tax liability.

pages.title: Can spouse W-2 withholding cover tax on my business income?
pages.seo_title: Spouse W-2 Withholding for Business Income
pages.description: On a joint-return projection, reconcile both spouses' income and withholding before choosing additional payments.

pages.title: Do I owe personal estimated tax when my S corporation keeps the cash?
pages.seo_title: S Corp Retained Earnings and Personal Estimated Tax
pages.description: Reconcile expected K-1 income with wages, shareholder basis and the corporation's cash needs.

pages.title: Should I reserve tax money from revenue or from profit?
pages.seo_title: Business Tax Reserve: Revenue vs Taxable Profit
pages.description: No. It can support cash discipline, but taxable profit and the household projection determine the actual funding need.

pages.title: Can I fix a missed estimated tax payment by paying extra later?
pages.seo_title: Missed Estimated Tax Payment: What a Later Payment Fixes
pages.description: Not automatically. Installment timing and applicable exceptions determine the result, rather than the annual total alone.

pages.title: Does extending my business return extend my tax payment deadline?
pages.seo_title: Business Return Extension vs Tax Payment Deadline
pages.description: Identify the corporation, partnership and individual filings involved and distinguish their filing extensions from payment requirements.

pages.title: How do rental property sales affect quarterly estimated taxes?
pages.seo_title: Rental Sale Estimated Taxes: Gain vs Closing Cash
pages.description: Use the sale price, selling costs, historical adjusted basis and depreciation records to calculate the tax items.

pages.title: Can I use last year's refund toward this year's business taxes?
pages.seo_title: Applying Last Year's Refund to Estimated Tax
pages.description: Read the filed return to see whether the overpayment was designated for refund, applied forward or split.

pages.title: What should an owner include in a midyear tax projection?
pages.seo_title: Midyear Tax Projection for Multiple Businesses
pages.description: Request current books for each company and property, year-to-date payroll, known investment events and prior carryforwards.

pages.title: Can I reimburse owner business expenses paid with a personal credit card?
pages.seo_title: Owner Personal Card Expenses: Corporate Reimbursement
pages.description: An owner expense report should identify the merchant, date, amount, business purpose and company that incurred the cost.

pages.title: Does an accountable plan let me deduct all my personal meals?
pages.seo_title: Accountable Plans and Personal Meals
pages.description: Separate ordinary personal meals from meals that qualify under the applicable business rules.

pages.title: Can my company reimburse mileage if I also use the car personally?
pages.seo_title: Mileage Reimbursement for a Mixed-Use Owner Vehicle
pages.description: Keep a log showing dates, destinations, business purposes and business miles, along with the records needed for the chosen method.

pages.title: How should I document a trip that mixes business and vacation?
pages.seo_title: Business Trip With Vacation: Expense Allocation
pages.description: Write down where the trip occurred, its primary purpose, business days, personal days and who traveled.

pages.title: Can I deduct commuting when I own the business?
pages.seo_title: Business Owner Commuting vs Business Mileage
pages.description: Map the home, regular workplace, temporary assignments and trips between work locations.

pages.title: Can I reimburse expenses without keeping paper receipts?
pages.seo_title: Electronic Expense Receipts: What Records Must Show
pages.description: A digital receipt should retain item detail, date, amount and merchant information.

pages.title: How should a business owner handle reimbursement advances?
pages.seo_title: Accountable Plan Travel Advances: Excess Cash
pages.description: Track the date and purpose of the advance, the expenses substantiated and the balance returned.

pages.title: Can I deduct travel to inspect a possible rental property?
pages.seo_title: Travel to Inspect a Potential Rental Property
pages.description: Record the properties visited, meetings, trip dates and reason for each expense.

pages.title: Can my company pay for my spouse to accompany me on business travel?
pages.seo_title: Spouse Business Travel: Employee Role and Purpose
pages.description: A spouse's airfare or lodging should not be included merely because the owner had a qualifying trip.

pages.title: What should I do when an owner expense report includes personal charges?
pages.seo_title: Personal Charges on Owner Expense Reports
pages.description: No. Profitability does not create a business deduction for personal spending.

pages.title: Can S corporation distributions fund my 401(k) contribution limit?
pages.seo_title: S Corp Distributions vs 401(k) Compensation
pages.description: Ask the plan administrator to identify eligible compensation under the actual document.

pages.title: Can I keep a solo 401(k) after hiring employees?
pages.seo_title: Solo 401(k) After Hiring Employees
pages.description: Send the administrator the hire dates, service hours, ages and ownership relationships of all workers.

pages.title: Should a cash balance plan be based on one unusually profitable year?
pages.seo_title: Cash Balance Plan After a One-Time Profit Spike
pages.description: Ask the actuary to show required funding under several profit scenarios and explain how employee costs change.

pages.title: Do employees change how much my retirement plan will cost?
pages.seo_title: Retirement Plan Employee Costs: Full Company Budget
pages.description: Request a proposal showing owner allocations, staff contributions, administration, actuarial costs and other fees separately.

pages.title: Can my spouse participate in my business retirement plan?
pages.seo_title: Spouse Eligibility for a Business Retirement Plan
pages.description: Document the spouse's duties, hours and reasonable compensation for actual services.

pages.title: Do two businesses give me two separate employee deferral limits?
pages.seo_title: Two Businesses and 401(k) Deferral Limits
pages.description: Identify all plans receiving employee deferrals, including plans at an unrelated W-2 job.

pages.title: Can rental income support a solo 401(k) contribution?
pages.seo_title: Rental Income and Solo 401(k) Eligibility
pages.description: Determine whether the receipts arise from ordinary investment rentals or an actual operating activity with different tax treatment.

pages.title: Is a deductible retirement contribution the same as tax-free retirement income?
pages.seo_title: Retirement Deduction vs Future Taxable Withdrawals
pages.description: Identify whether the contribution is deductible, Roth or after-tax under the actual plan.

pages.title: What should I do after contributing too much to a business retirement plan?
pages.seo_title: Excess Retirement Contribution: Correction Handoff
pages.description: Provide the administrator the plan document, compensation, deposits and contribution sources.

pages.title: What records should I give an actuary for a cash balance plan proposal?
pages.seo_title: Cash Balance Plan Proposal: Actuary Records
pages.description: Provide employee ages, compensation, hire dates, hours and ownership relationships across companies.

pages.title: Does guaranteeing my S corporation bank loan create debt basis?
pages.seo_title: S Corp Loan Guarantee vs Shareholder Debt Basis
pages.description: Read the loan documents to identify who borrowed and who advanced funds to the corporation.

pages.title: Can debt basis make an S corporation distribution tax-free?
pages.seo_title: S Corp Debt Basis and Cash Distributions
pages.description: Reconcile stock basis before analyzing the tax treatment of a distribution.

pages.title: Why can repayment of my shareholder loan create taxable income?
pages.seo_title: Shareholder Loan Repayment With Reduced Debt Basis
pages.description: Track the original advance, prior repayments, loss-related basis reductions and any later basis restoration.

pages.title: Can a bookkeeping loan entry cure an excess S corporation distribution?
pages.seo_title: Excess S Corp Distribution: Book Entry vs Actual Loan
pages.description: Examine the original payment, contemporaneous intent and enforceable repayment arrangement.

pages.title: Can I deduct my entire K-1 loss if the business lost money?
pages.seo_title: K-1 Loss Deduction: Basis and Other Limits
pages.description: A K-1 shows an allocated tax item, but does not by itself establish how much the owner can deduct.

pages.title: Should I track stock basis separately for each S corporation?

pages.description: Create a separate basis schedule for each ownership interest and reconcile it annually with K-1s, contributions, distributions and relevant adjustments.

pages.title: Do retained S corporation profits affect shareholder stock basis?
pages.seo_title: Retained S Corp Profits and Stock Basis
pages.description: Review K-1 income and the other annual basis adjustments rather than using retained earnings on the books as a shortcut.

pages.title: Can contributing cash before year-end support an S corporation loss?
pages.seo_title: Year-End Cash Contribution and S Corp Loss Basis

pages.title: What happens to S corporation losses suspended for lack of basis?
pages.seo_title: S Corp Basis-Suspended Losses: Carryforward Records
pages.description: Maintain the original loss amount, year, limitation and subsequent utilization for each corporation.

pages.title: What should Form 7203 reconcile to in my owner tax file?
pages.seo_title: Form 7203 Reconciliation: Shareholder Basis File
pages.description: The form should connect opening basis, K-1 items, contributions, distributions and qualifying shareholder debt activity.

pages.title: Is a refundable rental security deposit taxable when received?
pages.seo_title: Refundable Security Deposits vs Rental Income
pages.description: Read the lease to distinguish refundable security from advance rent or a nonrefundable charge.

pages.title: Is advance rent taxable before the tenant uses the property?
pages.seo_title: Advance Rent vs Refundable Tenant Deposits
pages.description: For a cash-method landlord, advance rent generally enters income when received, unlike a genuinely refundable security deposit.

pages.title: Do tenant-paid expenses count as rental income?
pages.seo_title: Tenant-Paid Landlord Expenses: Gross Rental Reporting
pages.description: Determine whether the tenant paid an expense the landlord was responsible for and whether the payment reduced rent owed.

pages.title: Can I deduct mortgage principal on a rental property?
pages.seo_title: Rental Mortgage Payment: Principal vs Interest
pages.description: Use the mortgage statement to separate principal, interest, escrow deposits and fees.

pages.title: Is replacing a rental roof a repair or an improvement?
pages.seo_title: Rental Roof Replacement: Repair or Improvement
pages.description: Obtain the contractor's detailed work description and distinguish patching from a substantial replacement or restoration.

pages.title: Can I depreciate land when I buy a rental property?
pages.seo_title: Land Allocation in Rental Property Depreciation
pages.description: Start with total acquisition cost and determine a reasonable allocation supported by relevant evidence.

pages.title: When does rental depreciation begin if renovations delay tenants?
pages.seo_title: Rental Depreciation Start Date During Renovations
pages.description: Build a timeline from closing through renovation completion, approvals, marketing and readiness for the intended rental use.

pages.title: Can I deduct rental expenses while the property is vacant?
pages.seo_title: Vacant Rental Expenses: Continued Rental Use
pages.description: Keep evidence that the property remains held for rental use, such as marketing, applications, management correspondence and efforts to obtain tenants.

pages.title: How does personal use of a vacation rental affect deductions?
pages.seo_title: Vacation Rental Personal Use: Day and Expense Records
pages.description: Track rented days, personal days, below-market use and days devoted to relevant maintenance activities.

pages.title: Do Airbnb platform fees reduce the rent I report?
pages.seo_title: Airbnb Gross Income vs Net Platform Deposits
pages.description: Download platform statements showing guest charges, owner-paid fees, refunds, adjustments and amounts handled for taxes.

pages.title: Is exactly 100 hours enough for the short-term rental participation test?
pages.seo_title: STR 100-Hour Test: Exactly 100 vs More Than 100
pages.description: For this test, distinguish more than 100 hours from exactly 100, then compare the taxpayer's participation with each other individual's participation.

pages.title: Do my spouse's hours count toward rental material participation?
pages.seo_title: Spouse Hours for Rental Material Participation
pages.description: Maintain the spouse's work record alongside the owner's record and identify actual services, dates and activity.

pages.title: Can my business partner's hours count as my participation?
pages.seo_title: Business Partner Hours vs Owner Participation
pages.description: Record which partner performed each task rather than allocating operating hours according to ownership percentages.

pages.title: Can I materially participate when I hire a property manager?
pages.seo_title: Airbnb Material Participation With a Property Manager
pages.description: Ask the manager to describe the services performed and how work is divided among individuals.

pages.title: Does an average guest stay of seven days make my rental loss deductible?
pages.seo_title: Seven-Day Average Stay vs Deductible STR Loss
pages.description: Calculate average customer use from the relevant rental periods and retain the reservation data.

pages.title: Does a real estate license automatically qualify me as a real estate professional?
pages.seo_title: Real Estate License vs Real Estate Professional Status
pages.description: Review qualifying real property trade or business services, the more-than-750-hour requirement and the more-than-half personal-services requirement.

pages.title: Can a full-time W-2 employee qualify as a real estate professional?
pages.seo_title: REPS With a Full-Time W-2 Job: Time Evidence
pages.description: Start with the actual outside-job schedule, including overtime and other personal services.

pages.title: Are investor research hours the same as rental participation hours?
pages.seo_title: Rental Investor Research Hours vs Operating Work
pages.description: Separate studying markets, monitoring investments and reviewing reports from substantive day-to-day operations.

pages.title: Can I combine every rental property to meet material participation?
pages.seo_title: Grouping Rental Activities for Material Participation
pages.description: List each property's ownership, use, activity classification and participation history.

pages.title: Does meeting material participation release every prior suspended loss?
pages.seo_title: Prior Passive Losses After Material Participation Changes
pages.description: Identify the origin of each suspended passive loss and whether the activity is now a former passive activity.

pages.title: Can a cost segregation report write off the entire rental purchase price?
pages.seo_title: Cost Segregation vs Writing Off the Entire Purchase
pages.description: Start with supported acquisition basis, remove nondepreciable land and identify later improvements or separately purchased assets.

pages.title: Can I use 100% bonus depreciation on a property acquired in 2026?
pages.seo_title: 100% Bonus Depreciation in 2026: Eligibility Review
pages.description: The restored 100% allowance generally concerns eligible property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025, subject to statutory requirements and applicable elections.

pages.title: Does a cost segregation deduction equal the refund I will receive?
pages.seo_title: Cost Segregation Deduction vs Tax Refund
pages.description: Ask for the study's identified depreciation separately from the amount currently usable on the return.

pages.title: Can I order a cost segregation study several years after buying?
pages.seo_title: Cost Segregation Several Years After Purchase
pages.description: Collect original closing records and all filed depreciation schedules before ordering implementation.

pages.title: Should furniture already on my asset schedule appear again in a cost segregation study?
pages.seo_title: Furniture in Cost Segregation: Prevent Double Counting
pages.description: It should not create duplicate basis or deductions. Reconcile the schedules and identify one supported treatment for each cost.

pages.title: Does the previous owner's cost segregation study determine my depreciation?
pages.seo_title: Previous Owner's Cost Segregation vs Buyer Basis
pages.description: A seller's report may contain useful property descriptions, but its tax basis, dates and elections belong to that taxpayer.

pages.title: Can I elect out of bonus depreciation after receiving a cost segregation study?
pages.seo_title: Electing Out of Bonus After a Cost Segregation Study
pages.description: A study identifies assets; it does not itself make a bonus-depreciation election.

pages.title: Does financing a property reduce the basis available for depreciation?
pages.seo_title: Financed Rental Purchase: Debt, Basis and Loss Limits
pages.description: A property purchase financed with genuine debt can include amounts beyond the down payment in acquisition basis.

pages.title: Can cost segregation help if my rental losses are currently passive?
pages.seo_title: Cost Segregation When Rental Losses Are Passive
pages.description: Estimate the deduction, then determine whether passive income or another applicable rule permits current use.

pages.title: What should I verify before implementing a cost segregation report?
pages.seo_title: Implementing a Cost Segregation Report: Return Checklist
pages.description: Match the taxpayer, property, supported basis, excluded land, acquisition costs and improvements to the final report version.

pages.title: Can I receive rental sale proceeds and arrange a 1031 exchange afterward?
pages.seo_title: Receiving Sale Proceeds Before a 1031 Exchange
pages.description: Talk with the qualified intermediary and tax adviser before selling, signing final instructions or directing proceeds.

pages.title: Does paying off my mortgage eliminate tax on a rental sale?
pages.seo_title: Rental Mortgage Payoff vs Taxable Sale Gain
pages.description: No. Debt repayment and taxable gain follow different calculations.

pages.title: Can I exchange real estate for business equipment under Section 1031?
pages.seo_title: Section 1031 Real Estate vs Business Equipment
pages.description: Current Section 1031 treatment applies to qualifying real property, not a general swap of business assets.

pages.title: Can a house bought primarily to flip qualify for a 1031 exchange?
pages.seo_title: House Flips and 1031 Exchange Eligibility
pages.description: Review acquisition plans, renovation activity, marketing, frequency of sales and actual use.

pages.title: Does a 1031 exchange permanently erase depreciation recapture?
pages.seo_title: 1031 Exchange and Future Depreciation Recapture
pages.description: A qualifying exchange can defer eligible gain, but is not a blanket promise to permanently erase depreciation-related tax.

pages.title: Can I buy replacement property in a different LLC?
pages.seo_title: 1031 Replacement Property in a Different LLC
pages.description: Determine how the selling owner and proposed buying entity are classified for federal tax purposes.

pages.title: What happens if I keep some cash in a 1031 exchange?
pages.seo_title: Keeping Cash in a 1031 Exchange: Recognized Gain
pages.description: Ask the preparer to show realized gain, recognized gain and deferred gain separately.

pages.title: Do 1031 exchange deadlines pause while I negotiate financing?
pages.seo_title: 1031 Deadlines and Financing Delays
pages.description: A deferred exchange generally has a 45-day identification period and completion by the earlier of 180 days or the relevant return due date including extensions.

pages.title: How do I calculate adjusted basis before selling a rental?
pages.seo_title: Adjusted Basis Before a Rental Sale
pages.description: Not ordinarily. Tax basis follows the actual acquisition and adjustment history, not simply current market value.

pages.title: Should I choose a 1031 exchange solely to avoid this year's tax?
pages.seo_title: 1031 Exchange vs Paying Tax: Investment Comparison
pages.description: Model the sale without an exchange alongside the proposed replacement acquisition.

pages.title: Is Form 3115 always required when depreciation was missed?
pages.seo_title: Missed Depreciation: Form 3115 or Amended Return?
pages.description: No. The facts and accounting-method history determine the appropriate correction route.

pages.title: Can I put all missed depreciation on this year's Schedule E?
pages.seo_title: Missed Rental Depreciation on Current Schedule E
pages.description: Prepare an asset-by-asset comparison showing what was claimed and what the correct treatment would have been.

pages.title: Does a new cost segregation report require amending every old return?
pages.seo_title: New Cost Segregation Report: Amend or Change Method?
pages.description: A study measures and classifies property, while return implementation requires a separate procedural decision.

pages.title: What is a Section 481(a) adjustment supposed to reconcile?
pages.seo_title: Section 481(a) Depreciation Adjustment: Reconciliation
pages.description: For the eligible method change, compare the amounts reflected under the old method with those under the proposed method at the required transition point.

pages.title: Can I claim a catch-up deduction after selling the rental?
pages.seo_title: Depreciation Catch-Up After Selling a Rental
pages.description: Provide the sale closing date, filed returns, extension status, asset schedules and proposed correction details.

pages.title: Can Form 3115 fix a missed bonus depreciation election automatically?
pages.seo_title: Form 3115 vs Missed Bonus Depreciation Election
pages.description: No. Asset analysis and election relief are separate matters with their own requirements.

pages.title: What records should I give my CPA for a depreciation correction?
pages.seo_title: Depreciation Correction Documents for a New CPA
pages.description: Request detailed depreciation reports from every preparer involved, including disposals, elections and carryforward schedules.

pages.title: Does a depreciation correction guarantee a refund?
pages.seo_title: Depreciation Correction vs Immediate Refund
pages.description: Start with the allowable correction and determine the tax year in which it is reported.

pages.title: Can I file a depreciation method change without coordinating entity returns?
pages.seo_title: Depreciation Method Change for Partnership-Owned Property
pages.description: Trace legal ownership and federal classification for the property and the return reporting its depreciation.

pages.title: How do I avoid counting a catch-up deduction twice?
pages.seo_title: Catch-Up Depreciation: Prevent Duplicate Deductions
pages.description: Keep separate columns for original basis, prior depreciation, the method-change adjustment and current-year depreciation.
